Cost of current investment acquired was ₹1,000 but the fair value was ₹800. The Investment was recorded at ₹800. Now the fair value of Investment is ₹1,200. At what value should it be recorded and how much gain will be credited to profit and loss account.

questions.questionHtml:
(a) A Ltd. provides after sales warranty for two years to its customers. Based on past experience, the company has the following policy for making provision for warranties on the invoice amount, on the remaining balance warranty period. Less than 1 year: 2% provision. More than 1 year: 3% provision.

The company has raised invoices as under:

Invoice DateAmount (₹)
11th Feb, 202260,000
25th Dec, 202240,000
04th Oct, 20231,35,000

Calculate the provision to be made for warranty under AS-29 as at 31st March, 2023 and 31st March, 2024. Also compute amount to be debited to P & L account for the year ended 31st March, 2024.

(b) As per provisions of AS-26, how would you deal with the following situations:

  1. ₹23,00,000 paid by a manufacturing company to the legal advisor for defending the patent of a product is treated as a capital expenditure.
  2. During the year 2023-24, a company spent ₹7,00,000 for publicity and research expenses on one of its new consumer products which was marketed in the same accounting year but proved to be a failure.
  3. A company spent ₹25,00,000 in the past three years to develop a product, these expenses were charged to profit and loss account since they did not meet AS-26 criteria for capitalization. In the current year approval of the concerned authority has been received. The company wishes to capitalize ₹25,00,000 by disclosing it as a prior period item.
  4. A company with a turnover of ₹200 crores and an annual advertising budget of ₹50,00,000 had taken up for the marketing of a new product by a company. It was estimated that the company would have a turnover of ₹20 crore from the new product. The company had debited to its Profit & Loss Account the total expenditure of ₹50,00,000 incurred on extensive special initial advertisement campaign for the new product.

(c) Indicate in each case whether revenue can be recognized and when it will be recognized as per AS-9:

  1. Trade discount and volume rebate received.
  2. Where goods are sold to distributors or others for resale.
  3. Where seller concurrently agrees to repurchase the same goods at a later date.
  4. Insurance agency commission for rendering services.
  5. On 11-03-2024 cloths worth ₹50,000 were sold to X mart, but due to refurbishing of their showroom being underway, on their request, clothes were delivered on 12-04-2024.
questions.answerHtml:
(a) Provision to be made for warranty under AS 29:

As at 31st March, 2023 = ₹60,000 × 0.02 + ₹40,000 × 0.03 = ₹1,200 + ₹1,200 = ₹2,400

As at 31st March, 2024 = ₹40,000 × 0.02 + ₹1,35,000 × 0.03 = ₹800 + ₹4,050 = ₹4,850

₹
Balance of provision required as on 31.03.20244,850
Less: Opening Balance as on 1.4.2023(2,400)
Amount debited to profit and loss account2,450

Note: No provision will be made on 31st March, 2024 in respect of sales amounting ₹60,000 made on 11th February, 2022 as the warranty period of 2 years has already expired.

(b) As per AS 26 'Intangible Assets', subsequent expenditure on an intangible asset after its purchase or completion should be recognised as an expense when incurred unless (a) it is probable that the expenditure will enable the asset to generate future economic benefits in excess of its originally assessed standard of performance, and (b) the expenditure can be measured and attributed to the asset reliably.

  1. The legal expenses of ₹23,00,000 to defend the patent should NOT be capitalized and should be charged to the Profit and Loss Statement.
  2. The company is required to expense the entire ₹7,00,000 in the P&L for the year ended 31st March 2024 because no benefit will arise in the future.
  3. Expenditure on an intangible item initially recognized as an expense in previous annual financial statements should NOT be recognized as part of the cost of an intangible asset at a later date. The company cannot capitalize ₹25,00,000 - it should remain recognized as an expense.
  4. Expenditure of ₹50,00,000 on advertising and promotional activities should always be charged to the P&L Statement. The company has done the correct treatment by debiting the sum to the P&L Account.

(c)

  1. Trade discounts and volume rebates received are not encompassed within the definition of revenue, since they represent a reduction of cost. Trade discounts and volume rebates given should be deducted in determining revenue.
  2. When goods are sold to a distributor or others, revenue can generally be recognized if significant risks of ownership have passed; however, in some situations the buyer may in substance be an agent, in which case the sale should be treated as a consignment sale.
  3. For transactions where the seller concurrently agrees to repurchase the same goods at a later date, that are in substance a financing agreement, the resulting cash inflow is not revenue as defined and should not be recognized as revenue.
  4. Insurance agency commissions should be recognized on the effective commencement or renewal dates of the related policies.
  5. On 11.03.2024, since X mart takes title and accepts billing for the goods, the sale is implied complete and all risk and reward of ownership has been transferred to the buyer. Revenue should be recognized for the year ended 31st March, 2024 notwithstanding that physical delivery has not been completed, so long as there is every expectation that delivery will be made and the items were ready for delivery to the buyer at the time.

(b) A Ltd. sold JCB having WDV of ₹20 lakhs to B Ltd. for ₹24 lakhs and the same JCB was leased back by B Ltd. to A Ltd. The lease is an operating lease. In context of Accounting Standard 19 'Leases' explain the accounting treatment of profit or loss in the books of A Ltd. if: (i) Sale price of ₹24 lakhs is equal to fair value. (ii) Fair value is ₹20 lakhs and sale price is ₹24 lakhs. (iii) Fair value is ₹22 lakhs and sale price is ₹25 lakhs. (iv) Fair value is ₹25 lakhs and sale price is ₹18 lakhs. (v) Fair value is ₹18 lakhs and sale price is ₹19 lakhs.

(c) Give Journal Entries in the books of Branch A to rectify or adjust the following: (i) Head Office expenses ₹3,500 allocated to the Branch, but not recorded in the Branch Books. (ii) Depreciation of branch assets, whose accounts are kept by the Head Office, not provided earlier for ₹1,500. (iii) Branch paid ₹2,000 as salary to a H.O. Inspector, but the amount paid has been debited by the Branch to Salaries account. (iv) H.O. collected ₹10,000 directly from a customer on behalf of the Branch, but no intimation to this effect has been received by the Branch. (v) A remittance of ₹15,000 sent by the Branch has not yet been received by the Head Office. (vi) Branch A incurred advertisement expenses of ₹3,000 on behalf of Branch B.

(a)

ElementDefinition
AssetResource controlled by the enterprise as a result of past events from which future economic benefits are expected to flow to the enterprise
LiabilityPresent obligation of the enterprise arising from past events, the settlement of which is expected to result in an outflow of a resource embodying economic benefits
EquityResidual interest in the assets of an enterprise after deducting all its liabilities
Income/gainIncrease in economic benefits during the accounting period in the form of inflows or enhancement of assets or decreases in liabilities that result in increase in equity other than those relating to contributions from equity participants
Expense/lossDecrease in economic benefits during the accounting period in the form of outflows or depletions of assets or incurrence of liabilities that result in decrease in equity other than those relating to distributions to equity participants

Or - Schedule III has come into force for the Balance Sheet and P&L prepared for financial years commencing on or after 1st April, 2023. As per Part I of Schedule III, a company should disclose in notes to accounts, for the period of 5 years immediately preceding the balance sheet date, the aggregate number and class of shares allotted as fully paid-up bonus shares. Schedule III does NOT require a company to disclose the source from which bonus shares have been issued. Therefore, non-disclosure of the source does NOT violate Schedule III to the Companies Act.

(b)

(a) State with reasons, how the following events would be dealt with in the financial statements of Hari Ltd. for the year ended 31st March, 2024 (accounts approved on 25th July, 2024):

  1. Negotiations with another company for acquisition of its business started on 21st January, 2024. Hari Ltd. invested ₹40 lakh on 22nd April, 2024.
  2. The company made a provision for bad debts @4% of its total debtors (trend from previous years). In the second week of March 2024, a debtor for ₹2,50,000 suffered heavy loss due to an earthquake; the loss was not insured. In May 2024 the debtor became bankrupt.
  3. During 2023-24, Hari Ltd. was sued by a competitor for ₹13 lakhs for infringement of a trademark. Based on legal counsel's advice, Hari Ltd. provided ₹8 lakhs in its financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 2024. On 26th May, 2024, the Court decided in favour of the competitor and ordered Hari Ltd. to pay ₹12 lakhs.
  4. Cashier of Hari Ltd. embezzled cash of ₹3,00,000 during March 2024; this came to the notice of management only in August 2024.
  5. Cheques dated 31st March, 2024 collected in April 2024, presented to the bank in April and also realized in the same month in the normal course after deposit.

(b) Honey Ltd. is developing a new production method. During the financial year ended 31st March, 2023, total expenditure incurred on development of this production method was ₹98,00,000. On 1st Jan, 2023, the production method met the criteria as an intangible asset and expenditure incurred till this date was ₹68,00,000. Further expenditure incurred on the new method was ₹72,00,000 for the year ended 31st March, 2024, and recoverable amount of the know-how embodied in the new method for this financial year is ₹52,00,000.

Calculate: (1) The carrying amount of the Intangible asset on 31st March, 2023. (2) The expenditure to be shown in Statement of Profit and Loss for the year ended 31st March, 2024. (3) The carrying amount of the Intangible asset on 31st March, 2024.
questions.answerHtml:
(a)

  1. As per AS 4, disclosure should be made in the report of the approving authority of events occurring after the balance sheet date representing material changes/commitments affecting financial position - the ₹40 lakh investment (April 2024) in acquisition of another company should be disclosed in the Board's report to enable users to make proper evaluations.
  2. As per AS 4, adjustment is required for events providing additional information materially affecting amounts relating to conditions existing at the Balance Sheet date. The debtor's earthquake loss was already known before year-end; the bankruptcy in May 2024 is only additional information on the existing condition. Full provision for bad debts of ₹2,50,000 should be made in the final accounts for the year ended 31st March 2024.
  3. As per AS 4, this is an adjusting event since the suit and its provision were already recognized during 2023-24; the Court's decision (26th May 2024, before approval of financial statements) constitutes additional evidence of the condition existing at the balance sheet date. Hari Ltd. should adjust the provision upward by ₹4 lakhs to reflect the Court-awarded penalty.
  4. Since the embezzlement came to management's notice only after board approval of the financial statements, it is treated per AS 5 'Net Profit or Loss for the Period, Prior Period Items and Changes in Accounting Policies' and is NOT adjusted in the financial statements for the year ended 31st March, 2024. As an extraordinary item, it should be disclosed in the statement of profit and loss as part of the loss for the year ending March 2025, in a manner showing its impact on current profit/loss.
  5. Collection of cheques after the balance sheet date is NOT an adjusting event, even if the cheques bear the date of 31st March. questions.questionHtml:
(a) Given the following information of Rainbow Ltd.:

  1. On 15th November, goods worth ₹5,00,000 were sold on approval basis. The approval period was 4 months, after which they were considered sold. Buyer sent approval for 75% of goods sold up to 31st January and no approval/disapproval for the rest till 31st March.
  2. On 31st March, goods worth ₹2,40,000 were sold to Bright Ltd. but due to refurbishing of their show-room, on their request, goods were delivered on 10th April.
  3. Rainbow Ltd. supplied goods worth ₹6,00,000 to Shyam Ltd. and concurrently agrees to re-purchase the same goods on 14th April.
  4. Dew Ltd. used certain assets of Rainbow Ltd. Rainbow Ltd. received ₹7.5 lakhs and ₹12 lakhs as interest and royalties respectively from Dew Ltd. during 2023-24.
  5. On 25th December, goods of ₹4,00,000 were sent on consignment basis, of which 40% remained unsold with the consignee at year-end (31st March).

In each case, advise, with valid reasons, the amount to be recognized as revenue under AS-9.

(b) The following information of Rocky Ltd. as at March 31, 2024 (₹ in lacs): Fully paid equity shares of ₹10 each 500; Capital Reserve 6; 12% Debentures 400; Debenture Interest Outstanding 48; Trade payables 165; Directors' Remuneration Outstanding 10; Other Outstanding Expenses 11; Provisions 33. Assets: Goodwill 15; Land and Building 184; Plant and Machinery 286; Furniture and Fixtures 41; Inventory 142; Trade receivables 80; Cash at Bank 27; Discount on Issue of Debentures 8; Profit and Loss Account (debit) 390.

Scheme of internal reconstruction approved by the Tribunal and implemented: (i) All equity shares converted into the same number of fully-paid equity shares of ₹2.50 each. (ii) Directors forego their outstanding remuneration. (iii) Debentureholders forego outstanding interest in return for 12% debentures being converted into 13% debentures. (iv) Existing shareholders subscribe for cash, fully paid equity shares of ₹2.50 each for ₹125 lacs. (v) Trade payables given option of either fully-paid equity shares of ₹2.50 each for the amount due, or 80% of the amount due in cash. Trade payables for ₹65 lacs accept equity shares; those for ₹100 lacs accept ₹80 lacs cash in full settlement. (vi) Assets revalued: Land and building 230; Plant and Machinery 220; Inventory 120; Trade receivables 76.

Pass Journal Entries for all the above transactions immediately after the reconstruction.
questions.answerHtml:
(a)

  1. As per AS 9, in case of goods sold on approval basis, revenue should not be recognized until formally accepted, an act adopting the transaction occurs, or the rejection time period has elapsed. Revenue should be recognized for the total sales of ₹5,00,000 as the time period for rejecting the goods had expired.
  2. The sale is complete but delivery postponed at buyer's request. The entity should recognize the entire sale of ₹2,40,000 for the year ended 31st March.
  3. Sale/repurchase agreements (seller concurrently agrees to repurchase the same goods at a later date) are in substance a financing agreement; the resulting cash inflow is not revenue as defined and should not be recognized. Hence no revenue recognized here.
  4. Revenue from use by others of enterprise resources yielding interest and royalty should be recognized when no significant uncertainty as to measurability/collectability exists. Interest should be recognized on time proportion basis; royalty on accrual basis per the agreement terms.
  5. 40% of goods lying unsold with consignee should be treated as closing inventory; sales should be recognized for ₹2,40,000 (60% of ₹4,00,000). In consignment sale, revenue is not recognized until goods are sold to a third party.

questions.questionHtml:
(a) "One of the characteristics of financial statements is neutrality" - Do you agree with this statement?

Or

What do you mean by Carve outs/ins in Ind AS? Explain.

(b) "The company has not made provision for warranty in respect of certain goods considering that the company can claim the warranty cost from the original supplier". Comment in line with the provisions of AS 29.

(c) Why are goods marked on invoice price by the head office while sending goods to the branch?
questions.answerHtml:
(a) Yes, one of the characteristics of financial statements is neutrality. To be reliable, information in financial statements must be neutral, i.e. free from bias. Financial Statements are not neutral if, by selection or presentation of information, the focus of analysis could shift from one area of business to another, arriving at a totally different conclusion on business results.

Or - Certain changes have been made in Ind AS considering India's economic environment, which differs from that presumed in existence by IFRS. These differences, being deviations from the accounting principles and practices stated in IFRS, are commonly known as 'Carve-outs'. Additional guidance given in Ind AS over and above what is given in IFRS is termed 'Carve-in'.

(b) As per AS 29 'Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets', where some or all of the expenditure required to settle a provision is expected to be reimbursed by another party, the reimbursement should be recognized when, and only when, it is virtually certain that reimbursement will be received if the enterprise settles the obligation. The reimbursement should be treated as a separate asset, not exceeding the amount of the provision.

The company had not made provision for warranty considering it can claim the cost from the original supplier. However, the provision for warranty should have been made per AS 29, and the amount claimable as reimbursement should be treated as a SEPARATE ASSET in the financial statements, rather than omitting disclosure of the liability altogether. The accounting treatment adopted by the company is therefore NOT correct.

(c) Goods are marked on invoice price to achieve the following objectives: (i) To keep secret from the branch manager the cost price of the goods and profit made, so the branch manager may not start a rival/competitive business; (ii) To have effective control on stock - stock at any time must equal opening stock plus goods received from head office minus sales made at branch; (iii) To dictate pricing policy to its branches, and save work at branch since prices have already been decided.
